blocks.content:
The State Executive consists of:
• Governor
• Chief Minister
• Council of Ministers
• Advocate General of the State
The State Executive consists of:• Governor• Chief Minister• Council of Ministers• Advocate General of the State

items: The Advocate General of the State IS a part of the State Executive; questions frequently try to trick candidates by excluding this office.
Be prepared to identify all four constitutional components of the State Executive in multiple-choice questions.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The State Executive is composed of four distinct constitutional entities.
The Governor acts as the nominal head within the State Executive framework.
The Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers exercise real executive power in the state.
The Advocate General of the State is explicitly included as an integral part of the State Executive.
